item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=computational+frameworks+for+automated+axiom+falsification+in+autonomous+systems&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-2600-0413-5.ch003\", \"title\": [\"The Proliferation of Autonomous Cyber Weapons?\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous cyber weapons mark a major shift in digital conflict by compressing the cycle of observation, analysis, decision, and action while expanding the scale of possible offensive effects. This chapter examines their proliferation as a socio-technical and strategic phenomenon rather than a technical programming issue. It defines autonomous cyber weapons as systems able to sense digital environments, reason over goals and constraints, choose among actions, and execute bounded cyber effects with limited or delayed human intervention. Drawing on scholarship in cybersecurity, adversarial machine learning, cyber conflict, and ethics, the chapter proposes a layered framework showing how data pipelines, knowledge graphs, model-based reasoning, action selection, and feedback loops can form offensive agentic. It also explains how these systems may intensify asymmetric warfare by reducing labor demands, accelerating operations, lowering coordination costs, and supporting continual adaptation, then concludes with governance, oversight, testing, escalation control, and resilient defense.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-2600-0413-5.ch003\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 29]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.22399/ijcesen.5196\", \"title\": [\"Agentic AI Frameworks: Building Autonomous, Self-Healing Systems for Financial Infrastructure\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Financial infrastructure management is facing unprecedented challenges as distributed architectures with hundreds of interdependent microservices impose complexity beyond the human cognitive limit for real-time monitoring and intervention. Conventional reactive monitoring systems bring intolerable latency between anomaly discovery and human perception, and the manual diagnostic processes take considerable time during which the services are degraded.
